lc_person: Alan Ford (born 1956), historian of Irish church history, University of Nottingham Department of Theology; author of The Protestant Reformation in Ireland.
item_person: Alan Ford, architect and author of books on school design; Wikidata states birth year 1952.

evidence.says: The authority heading is Ford, Alan, 1956-. Its source note for The Protestant Reformation in Ireland (1985) reports that the author information on the back cover gives 1956 as the birth year. A second source identifies the editor of Newes from the holy ile with the Department of Theology, Nottingham University.

The English description identifies an architect, with birth year 1952 and occupation architect (Q42973). The item nevertheless carries LC identifier n85327545 and VIAF identifier 56750979. Its sitelinks identify the architect.
The graph-linked author record is Ford, Alan, with birth year 1956.

The author record lists The protestant reformation in Ireland, 1590-1641, The origins of sectarianism in early modern Ireland, and As by law established. The first title matches the work cited by LC, supporting the LC-to-graph identification.

Oxford University Press identifies Alan Ford, Professor of Theology at the University of Nottingham, as author of James Ussher: Theology, History, and Politics in Early-Modern Ireland and England (2007).

The architectural practice identifies Alan Ford as author of books on school design, including Designing the Sustainable School and A Sense of Entry, distinguishing his work from that of the historian in LC.
The National Library of Ireland catalogue credits The Protestant Reformation in Ireland, 1590-1641 (1997 edition) to Ford, Alan, 1956-, corroborating the LC birth year and work identification.

notes: The item combines the architect identity with identifiers for the historian. This is a person mismatch, not evidence for changing the historian birth year to 1952. LC itself links to Q4706635, but its work and affiliation notes identify the historian. No separate Wikidata item for the LC person was verified.
